## Project Overview

This notebook prepares **CYBHI EBP/CDEP** Parental Stress Scale (PSS) assessment data for analysis and reporting. It ingests the raw eInsight export, processes the two-row hierarchical headers, maps text responses to numeric values, applies reverse scoring, computes total scores, and pairs each client's initial assessment with their last follow-up.

**Data source:** `PSS.csv` — eInsight Individual Assessments export.

**Scoring:**

- 18 items. Responses are stored as text and mapped to numeric values (case- and whitespace-insensitive): Strongly Disagree = 1, Disagree = 2, Undecided = 3, Agree = 4, Strongly Agree = 5. Any response that does not match is listed in Section 1.
- Items 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 17, and 18 are **reverse scored** using the formula `6 − raw_score`.
- Total score range: 18–90. Higher scores indicate greater parenting stress.
- **A lower follow-up score indicates a positive outcome.**
- Total score is set to `NA` if 2 or more items are missing. With 1 missing item the total is the sum of the 17 answered items (not prorated).
- **Contradictory forms:** a form is flagged when its answers disagree on average with both the 8 positive items and the 10 stress items (mean answer ≤ `pss_contradiction_cutoff`, default 2 = Disagree, on each set, before reversal). Such forms cannot be scored as answered. By default they are dropped before pairing (`pss_drop_contradictory <- TRUE`), so a client's initial or follow-up is their first or last usable form. Section 1 shows how many were flagged, by provider.

**Pairing logic:** Clients are grouped by `client_system_id`. The first assessment is the initial; the last assessment (if ≥2 assessments exist) is the follow-up. Clients with only one assessment are excluded. No minimum gap is enforced; `days_since_initial` is included so a gap rule can be applied downstream.

**Output:**

| File | Contents |
|----|----|
| `pss_paired_clean.csv` | One row per client: initial/follow-up scores, `positive_outcome`, `score_change`, quarter labels, `days_since_initial`, `initial_contradictory`, `follow_up_contradictory` (always `FALSE` when contradictory forms are dropped) |

# Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(zoo)

# ---- Configuration: edit paths and reporting window here ----
in_dir  <- "/Users/cristin/CWS Dropbox/Cristin Young/CYBHI Project/Data/eInsight Exports/Individual Assessments"
out_dir <- "/Users/cristin/CWS Dropbox/Cristin Young/CYBHI Project/Rebecca and Tristan and Cristin/EInsight Data"

start_date <- as.Date("2024-01-01")
end_date   <- Sys.Date()   # set to a fixed date (e.g., as.Date("2026-09-30")) to freeze the data window

# Contradictory forms: mean answer at or below the cutoff (2 = Disagree) on both the
# positive and the stress items. Set pss_drop_contradictory to FALSE to keep them
# (they stay flagged in the output).
pss_contradiction_cutoff <- 2
pss_drop_contradictory   <- TRUE
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Helper Functions

```{r helpers}
# ---- Shared helpers (identical across the cleaning scripts) ----

# Reads an eInsight assessment CSV export with two-row headers.
# Row 1 holds question text (merged cells export as blanks and are forward-
# filled); row 2 holds sub-headers ("Response", "Score", ...). Returns a data
# frame with combined snake_case names and fully blank columns removed.
# "0" is deliberately NOT treated as missing: it is a valid rating on most tools.
read_assessment_csv <- function(path, na_vals = c("-", "", "NA", "N/A")) {
  raw <- read_csv(path, na = na_vals, col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE,
                  col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

  h1    <- unlist(raw[1, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h2    <- unlist(raw[2, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h1_ff <- na.locf(h1, na.rm = FALSE) |> str_squish()

  new_names <- ifelse(
    is.na(h1_ff) | h1_ff == "",
    h2,
    paste(h1_ff, h2, sep = " - ")
  )
  new_names <- janitor::make_clean_names(new_names)

  df <- raw[-c(1, 2), ]
  names(df) <- new_names

  df |> select(where(~ !all(is.na(.))))
}

# Parses eInsight date strings in ISO (2024-03-15) or US (03/15/2024) format,
# with or without a time stamp. Warns with a count of non-blank values that
# could not be parsed (these become NA and are dropped by the date filter).
parse_einsight_date <- function(x, label = "date_completed") {
  x   <- na_if(str_squish(as.character(x)), "")
  out <- as.Date(parse_date_time(
    x,
    orders = c("Ymd", "mdY", "mdy", "Ymd HMS", "Ymd HM", "mdY HMS", "mdY HM"),
    quiet  = TRUE
  ))
  n_bad <- sum(!is.na(x) & is.na(out))
  if (n_bad > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_bad, " non-blank value(s) could not be parsed as dates and were set to NA.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  out
}

# Removes demo/test rows (provider_id or client_system_id contains "DEMO") and
# rows with no client_system_id (they cannot be linked or paired). Rows with a
# missing provider_id are kept. Prints a count for each.
remove_demo_rows <- function(df, label) {
  missing_ids <- setdiff(c("provider_id", "client_system_id"), names(df))
  if (length(missing_ids) > 0) {
    stop(label, ": column(s) needed for the demo filter not found: ",
         paste(missing_ids, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  is_demo   <- coalesce(str_detect(df$provider_id, "DEMO"), FALSE) |
               coalesce(str_detect(df$client_system_id, "DEMO"), FALSE)
  no_client <- is.na(df$client_system_id) & !is_demo
  cat(label, "- rows read:", nrow(df),
      "| DEMO rows removed:", sum(is_demo),
      "| rows with no client_system_id removed:", sum(no_client),
      "| rows with missing provider_id (kept):", sum(is.na(df$provider_id) & !is_demo & !no_client), "\n")
  df[!is_demo & !no_client, ]
}

# Stops if the number of item columns differs from what scoring expects.
# Scoring is positional, so a missing or extra column would silently shift
# reverse-scored items and weights onto the wrong questions.
check_items <- function(cols, expected, label) {
  if (length(cols) != expected) {
    stop(label, ": expected ", expected, " item columns but found ", length(cols), ":\n  ",
         paste(cols, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  message(label, ": found ", expected, " item columns as expected.")
  invisible(cols)
}

# Maps text responses to numbers, ignoring case and extra whitespace
# (e.g., "Strongly Disagree", "strongly disagree " and "Strongly disagree" all match).
map_responses <- function(x, map) {
  keys <- str_to_lower(str_squish(names(map)))
  unname(map[match(str_to_lower(str_squish(x)), keys)])
}

# Lists non-blank responses that do not match the scoring map. These would
# otherwise become NA silently and be counted as missing items.
# Returns the unmatched values (empty table = everything matched).
audit_unmapped <- function(df, cols, map, label) {
  keys <- str_to_lower(str_squish(names(map)))
  bad  <- df |>
    select(all_of(cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), values_to = "value") |>
    filter(!is.na(value), !str_to_lower(str_squish(value)) %in% keys) |>
    count(value, name = "n_values", sort = TRUE)
  if (nrow(bad) > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", sum(bad$n_values), " non-blank response(s) did not match the scoring map ",
            "and are treated as missing (see table).", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all non-blank responses match the scoring map.")
  }
  bad
}

# After reverse scoring, every item should correlate positively with the sum of
# the anchor items (excluding itself). Pass the items the instrument never
# reverse-scores as `anchor`: comparing against all items can hide a block of
# reversed items that mostly agree with each other. A negative value means the
# item's direction is wrong (reversed twice, or a positively worded item that
# was not reversed). Returns only the items that need a look (empty = all fine).
item_rest_check <- function(df, cols, label, anchor = cols) {
  anchor_sum <- rowSums(df[anchor], na.rm = TRUE)
  out <- tibble(
    item        = cols,
    item_rest_r = map_dbl(cols, function(col) {
      rest <- anchor_sum - if (col %in% anchor) coalesce(df[[col]], 0) else 0
      suppressWarnings(cor(df[[col]], rest, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
    })
  )
  n_neg <- sum(out$item_rest_r < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_neg > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_neg, " item(s) correlate negatively with the rest of the scale; ",
            "check reverse scoring (see table).", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all item-rest correlations are positive.")
  }
  out |> filter(item_rest_r < 0 | is.na(item_rest_r))
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Read and Score

```{r pss-read}
pss_raw <- read_assessment_csv(file.path(in_dir, "PSS.csv")) |>
  remove_demo_rows("PSS")

# Reverse-scored item positions (1-indexed within response columns)
rev_idx       <- c(1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 17, 18)
response_cols <- names(pss_raw)[endsWith(names(pss_raw), "_response")]
check_items(response_cols, 18, "PSS")

# Map text responses to numeric values
response_map <- c(
  "Strongly disagree" = 1,
  "Disagree"          = 2,
  "Undecided"         = 3,
  "Agree"             = 4,
  "Strongly agree"    = 5
)

pss_items <- pss_raw |>
  mutate(across(all_of(response_cols), ~ map_responses(.x, response_map))) |>
  mutate(
    # Disagrees on average with both the positive and the stress items (answers before reversal)
    contradictory = (rowMeans(across(all_of(response_cols[rev_idx])),  na.rm = TRUE) <= pss_contradiction_cutoff &
                     rowMeans(across(all_of(response_cols[-rev_idx])), na.rm = TRUE) <= pss_contradiction_cutoff) %in% TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(response_cols[rev_idx]), ~ 6 - .x))

pss_scores <- pss_items |>
  mutate(
    missing_count  = rowSums(is.na(across(all_of(response_cols)))),
    total_score    = rowSums(across(all_of(response_cols)), na.rm = TRUE),
    total_score    = if_else(missing_count >= 2, NA_real_, total_score),
    date_completed = parse_einsight_date(date_completed)
  ) |>
  select(client_system_id, provider_id, collection, date_completed, total_score, contradictory) |>
  filter(between(date_completed, start_date, end_date))

cat("Contradictory forms in window:", sum(pss_scores$contradictory), "of", nrow(pss_scores),
    if (pss_drop_contradictory) "(dropped before pairing)" else "(kept and flagged)", "\n")

pss_scores <- pss_scores |>
  filter(!(pss_drop_contradictory & contradictory))

cat("PSS rows after scoring:", nrow(pss_scores), "\n")
cat("Unique clients:        ", n_distinct(pss_scores$client_system_id), "\n")
cat("Missing total_score:   ", sum(is.na(pss_scores$total_score)), "\n")
```

Contradictory forms by provider, within the reporting window (providers with at least one):

```{r pss-contradictory}
pss_items |>
  mutate(date_completed = suppressWarnings(parse_einsight_date(date_completed))) |>
  filter(between(date_completed, start_date, end_date)) |>
  group_by(provider_id) |>
  summarise(
    n_forms           = n(),
    n_contradictory   = sum(contradictory),
    pct_contradictory = round(100 * mean(contradictory), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n_contradictory > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(n_contradictory))
```

Responses that did not match the scoring map (an empty table means every non-blank response was scored):

```{r pss-unmapped}
audit_unmapped(pss_raw, response_cols, response_map, "PSS")
```

Direction check after reverse scoring (an empty table means every item correlates positively with the rest of the scale):

```{r pss-direction}
item_rest_check(filter(pss_items, !(pss_drop_contradictory & contradictory)),
                response_cols, "PSS", anchor = response_cols[-rev_idx])
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Pair Initial and Follow-up

```{r pss-pair}
pss_paired <- pss_scores |>
  group_by(client_system_id) |>
  arrange(date_completed, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    n_assessments   = n(),
    initial_date    = first(date_completed),
    initial_score   = first(total_score),
    follow_up_date  = if_else(n_assessments >= 2, last(date_completed),  as.Date(NA)),
    follow_up_score = if_else(n_assessments >= 2, last(total_score),     NA_real_),
    initial_contradictory   = first(contradictory),
    follow_up_contradictory = if_else(n_assessments >= 2, last(contradictory), NA),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(follow_up_date)) |>
  mutate(
    # Lower follow-up score = positive outcome (lower stress is better)
    # 1 = improved, 0 = no change, -1 = worsened
    positive_outcome = case_when(
      follow_up_score <  initial_score ~ 1L,
      follow_up_score == initial_score ~ 0L,
      follow_up_score >  initial_score ~ -1L
    ),
    score_change       = follow_up_score - initial_score,
    initial_quarter    = paste0("Q", quarter(initial_date),    " ", year(initial_date)),
    follow_up_quarter  = paste0("Q", quarter(follow_up_date), " ", year(follow_up_date)),
    days_since_initial = as.integer(follow_up_date - initial_date)
  ) |>
  relocate(initial_contradictory, follow_up_contradictory, .after = last_col())

cat("PSS paired clients:", nrow(pss_paired), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Quick Check

```{r pss-check}
pss_paired |>
  summarise(
    n_paired           = n(),
    n_improved         = sum(positive_outcome ==  1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_no_change        = sum(positive_outcome ==  0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_worsened         = sum(positive_outcome == -1, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_improved       = round(100 * n_improved / n_paired, 1),
    n_missing_outcome  = sum(is.na(positive_outcome)),
    n_fu_within_3_days = sum(days_since_initial <= 3, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

# 4. Write Clean CSV

```{r write-csv}
write_csv(pss_paired, file.path(out_dir, "pss_paired_clean.csv"))

cat("CSV written successfully.\n")
```
